Header: Papaya ringspot virus ( syn. papaya distortion mosaic virus ) Papaya PRSV-strain

Prevention: Transplant healthy, clean virus-free papaya seedlings after 10-15 days manure application of 30-50g of cow dung per hole to improve growth vigour to reach maturity between 6-9 month.
Do not grow cucurbits nearby because they are hosts of the virus and harbour aphids which transmit the disease.
Avoid growing nearby bottle gourd, bitter gourd, pumpkins, squashes, ridge gourd, sponge gourd, cucumber as they harbour aphids’ vectors.
Plant aphid repellent crops such as onion, garlic and marigold between rows and maize around of orchards to reduce virus spread
Monitoring: Papaya ringspot virus is a papaya disease that is transmitted by aphids.
Monitor symptoms of the virus right from the nursery bed, then every 14 days after transplanting up to fruiting.
Look for the mosaic patterns of yellow and green with distortions on leaves.
Look for dark-green sunken oily ringspots on fruits caused by the virus.
Scout underside of leaves every 3 days for aphids 1 week after planting if the virus is known from the neighbouring fields.
The adult female aphid is yellow, 3 mm long and 1 to 2 mm wide covered with a white waxy coating.
Males are often pink, or yellow when young.
Consider control when 1-3 aphid colonies (vectors) are seen per papaya plant if the disease is known from neighbouring fields or when early symptoms of the virus are detected in your field
Action is too late for a plant that shows virus symptoms, as the plant cannot be cured.
Direct Control: Remove weak infected plants and bury them outside the farm or burn them to minimize the transmission of infection to healthy plants.
Regular weeding to reduce the population of aphids (vectors)

Conserve natural enemies of the aphids such as the ladybird beetles, lacewings, hover flies by growing flowers and herbs such as cilantro, dill, fennel, caraway, yarrow, and by not spaying insecticides.
Restrictions: Viruses are not controlled by pesticides.
Aphids (vectors) which transmit the virus diseases can be controlled by insecticides.
When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
